name: Technology & SaaS
core_perception: An abstract product judged on clarity, competence and whether the buyer believes it will work with what they already use. The main enemy is vagueness — the audience wants to know exactly what it does and what it costs before it will look at anything else.
visual_traits: screen and interface content as primary imagery
restrained palette with a single semantic accent
communication_needs: state the function in plain language before any benefit claim
show the product rather than describe it abstractly
composition: Modular and stacked with a strong opening statement and a visible next action. Interface fragments used as evidence outperform abstract technology imagery by a wide margin.
typography: Neutral sans across the hierarchy with a compact scale. Technical terms and product nouns must be set precisely; expressive display type reduces perceived competence in this category.
color: Neutral surfaces with semantic accent roles. Colour is used to indicate state and action rather than to create atmosphere, and contrast floors are set by accessibility requirements.
imagery: Real interface content, diagrams and data views. Abstract glowing-network imagery is the category's most persistent cliché and communicates nothing verifiable.
avoid: Abstract technology metaphors — glowing nodes, circuit patterns, floating holograms — which carry no information and are indistinguishable between competitors.
Emotional lifestyle imagery with no product presence, which delays the only question the buyer is actually asking.
Decorative or confrontational typography, which reads as a lack of engineering seriousness.
